use_case.name: oidc
use_case.title: oidc: an agent that acts as a signed-in user and never holds their tokens
use_case.summary: A folder with an AGENTS.md, deployed as a bundle; the agent has no sandbox. Its one connector is managed: it holds a bmc_v1 token and nothing else. Behind that connector a broker (the stand-in for Beyond's managed endpoint) signs each user in once with authorization code + PKCE against a real identity provider (Keycloak), keeps their refresh token sealed under a per-tenant key, refreshes the 60-second access tokens itself, and calls a notes service that trusts only a validated JWT. The checks drive two users through it, then look for any token in the agent.

tree.text:
---
model: gpt-4.1-mini
tools: mcp__notes__my_notes, mcp__notes__add_note
max-steps: 6
---

You are Sage, a notes assistant for one signed-in person. You have no shell and no sandbox: only a notes
service, reached through a connector that acts as whoever is signed in. You do not know who that is, and
you never see a password or a token.

- Answer in at most four sentences, plain text, no markdown.
- To read the person's notes call `my_notes`. Quote what it returns exactly, including any reference code.
- To add a note call `add_note`.
- When a tool returns an error, quote its message in your own answer, word for word, and say whether
  anything else is wrong. Never guess at what a tool would have said, and never retry a refused call.
- Use only the tools you were asked to use, and do nothing when the person asks for no tool.

bundle.store: a private S3 bucket (beyond-ai-demo-oidc-bundles-123456789012), fetched with a presigned link

checks.name: user-signs-in-once
checks.title: A user signs in once, and the broker holds the refresh token sealed
checks.detail: alice and bob each signed in once through the provider's login and consent pages (authorization code + PKCE S256); the broker holds each refresh token sealed (XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a per-tenant key: it opens under the tenant's key, not another's, and the plaintext is not in the file); each granted notes:read and offline_access, not notes:write; each session is bound to exactly its user's connection

at_rest.cipher: XChaCha20-Poly1305, key = HKDF-SHA256(master, tenant), aad = connection id
XChaCha20-Poly1305, key = HKDF-SHA256(master, tenant), aad = connection id

checks.name: agent-acts-as-user
checks.title: The agent acts as the user: the service sees the user's sub in a validated token
checks.detail: the model called the notes tool; the service validated a JWT (signature via JWKS, issuer, audience notes-api, expiry, scope notes:read) whose sub is alice's (11111111-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-111111111111) and returned alice's notes; the reply quotes her reference PR-109a0bc7

checks.name: agent-never-sees-token
checks.title: The agent never holds an access or refresh token
checks.detail: 4 real token tails (every access and refresh token the broker handled for the two users) were looked for in the grant, the agent's env, its logs (5 lines), both transcripts, the sealed session files and 1044 MB of its memory: none found. The planted control was found in memory (11) and in the transcript (1), so the scans do see what is there

measurements.grant: only a bmc_v1 bearer; no JWT text

checks.name: token-refresh
checks.title: The access token lapses and the broker refreshes it, invisibly to the agent
checks.detail: bob's first call used access token ofrtrt:74b7ad41-645e-e493-70fe-cb0b58baa1e6 (60s lifetime); after it lapsed the second call still worked: the broker refreshed (1792862112>1792862046), the notes service saw a new token ofrtrt:eabb4fd4-ae3a-40c9-f011-99d074c41de3, and the agent saw only the same answer (PR-41a93904) through the same bmc_v1 token

checks.name: users-isolated
checks.title: Two users in two sessions each see only their own data
checks.detail: alice's session saw only alice's notes (PR-109a0bc7) and bob's only bob's (PR-41a93904); every broker call of a session used that user's connection; alice's own token could not reach bob's connection by any route (named in a header or the URL, a token for an unconnected session, another connector, re-binding), and the service itself refused a request for another user's notes

attempts_with_alices_token.attempt: names bob's connection in a header
attempts_with_alices_token.answer: {"error":"this session's token is not bound to that connection"}

attempts_with_alices_token.attempt: names bob's connection in the URL
attempts_with_alices_token.answer: {"error":"this session's token is not bound to that connection"}

attempts_with_alices_token.attempt: a valid token for a session nobody connected
attempts_with_alices_token.answer: {"id":1,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"No user has connected their account to this session, so there is nothing to act as. The user has to sign i

attempts_with_alices_token.attempt: the token, aimed at another connector

checks.name: scope-enforced
checks.title: A tool needing a scope the connection lacks is refused upstream
checks.detail: add_note needs notes:write; alice's connection was granted only notes:read. The notes service (not the broker, not the agent) refused it for the missing scope, the tool returned "insufficient_scope… notes:write… not granted", the model told the user, and no note was written (reading back shows none)

measurements.tool_error: tool execution failed: insufficient_scope: add_note needs the notes:write scope, which this connection was not granted (it has: openid offline_access notes:read). The user would have to reconnect and approve it.
measurements.model_reply: The attempt to add the note "buy milk" failed because the connection lacks the necessary notes:write scope. The user would have to reconnect and approve it.

checks.name: revocation
checks.title: After the user revokes, the next call says so and the session survives
checks.detail: the user revoked: the broker asked the provider to revoke the refresh token (RFC 7009) and proved it dead (using it gets invalid_grant), then erased the stored copy; alice's next call returned a plain message that the connection was revoked and the model relayed it; her session kept running (it answered afterwards), and bob's connection was untouched

measurements.tool_message: tool execution failed: The connection to this account is no longer active: the user revoked this connection. The user has to sign in again to reconnect it; nothing else is wrong and the session is fine.
measurements.model_reply: The connection to this account is no longer active because the user revoked it. The user has to sign in again to reconnect; nothing else is wrong and the session is fine.

detail.reason: request named a connection this session is not bound to
request named a connection this session is not bound to
no connection bound to this session
